Abstract:

Among the various components of a spintronics device, spin manipulation is one of the most&nbspimportant aspect, as it determines the tunability of electron&rsquos spin degree of freedom. In this&nbspthesis, we intend to find non-magnetic spintronics material for spin manipulation. Among the&nbspvarious physical criteria governing spintronic functionality, spin-splitted band structure emerges&nbspas the most foundational requirement. This serves as the primary mechanism for generating and&nbsptuning spin-polarised states without dependence on an external global magnetic field. Band&nbspstructure calculations can be obtained from first principle studies using DFT. A tight-binding&nbspHamiltonian can be systematically derived by comparison with band structures that derived&nbspfrom first principle calculation. This Hamiltonian framework enables the calculation of several&nbspparameters, including spin to charge conversion efficiency, anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC),&nbspspin transfer torque, and other fundamental properties. To accomplish the objectives of this&nbspthesis work, we study the bulk altermagnetic material FeSb2&nbspas a prototypical material. DFT&nbspcalculations are performed using Quantum Esspresso, and the resulting band structure is used&nbspto construct the TB-Hamiltonian using Wannier90. The generated Hamiltonian is then used to calculate AHC. The computed AHC is found to vanish in the absence of the relativistic&nbspeffect. This ensures the reliability of the adopted computational framework. This thesis work&nbspthus establishes a systematic methodology for identifying non-magnetic materials and observing&nbspdevice-level parameters for spintronic device applications.
